source_name: SETCCE - novice (trusted digital transactions for financial institutions)
why_relevant: Slovenian e-signature / trust-services vendor selling digital onboarding and signing into financial institutions. Its Slovenian news items are compliance-marketing tied to eIDAS, ZEPEP/ZEPT and remote-onboarding (KYC) rules, and often name financial-sector deployments.

source_name: SRC d.o.o. - Rešitve za bančništvo in finance
why_relevant: Large Slovenian systems integrator with a dedicated banking/finance solution line (document capture, compliant long-term archiving, e-signature, digital identification, 'skladnost z zakonodajo'). Its solution pages describe exactly which regulatory obligations SI banks are outsourcing, and it is a likely incumbent at multiple private banks.

source_name: Mikrografija d.o.o. - blog / novice (certified e-archiving, mSef, mDocs)
why_relevant: Slovenian e-archiving vendor certified by Arhiv RS for capture and long-term storage; sells into regulated financial entities. Certification and product news date compliance obligations under ZVDAGA and sectoral record-keeping rules, and identify who audits/certifies bank archiving.

source_name: ASEE (Asseco South Eastern Europe) - banking sector pages and press releases
why_relevant: ASEE is a major SEE banking-software group whose portfolio explicitly includes 'reporting systems for regulatory compliance' and risk management, and whose Slovenian subsidiary (formerly Asseco SEE d.o.o., now Payten d.o.o., Ljubljana) sells into SI banks. Listed-company reporting plus sector pages give both contract signals and regulatory-product signals.

source_name: Payten (ASEE group) - payments vendor site, incl. Payten d.o.o. Ljubljana
why_relevant: Card/ATM/POS/e-commerce vendor with a Slovenian operating entity (Payten, informacijske rešitve in storitve, d.o.o., Litostrojska cesta 44C, Ljubljana; former names ASSECO SEE d.o.o. and SIMT CARDINFO). Local revenue ~EUR 12.8m (2024) indicates substantial SI bank/merchant contracts; site news and reference lists reveal card-scheme and PSD2/SCA compliance projects.

source_name: Comtrade programske rešitve d.o.o. (Ljubljana) - banking/finance projects
why_relevant: Ljubljana-registered software house (Letališka cesta 29B) with documented financial-sector delivery, e.g. an e-portal and financing-process application for SID banka. Useful for mapping who builds regulatory/reporting software for SI financial institutions; its public-procurement trail (SID, state entities) also reveals capabilities sold privately to commercial banks.

source_name: si.openprocurements.com - supplier profiles (Slovenian public procurement mirror)
why_relevant: Private SI banks do not tender publicly, but their vendors also serve SID banka, Banka Slovenije and state bodies. Supplier profiles here expose the vendor roster, contract values and subject matter, letting you infer which firms have bank-grade regulatory/IT capability in Slovenia.

source_name: Tricikel d.o.o. - DORA / ICT risk consultancy content (sl)
why_relevant: Domestic ICT/GRC consultancy publishing Slovenian-language DORA explainers aimed at financial entities and their ICT suppliers. Local consultancies name the concrete national interplay (e.g. ZInfV-1) that global vendors omit.

source_name: Akademija Finance - regulatory training events (ZInfV-1 in DORA)
why_relevant: Event agendas list the consultants, law firms, vendors and bank compliance officers actually working DORA/ZInfV-1 in Slovenia, with dates. Speaker lists are one of the cheapest ways to snowball the SI regtech supplier map and to date deadline pressure.

source_name: INFOSEK conference (Nova Gorica) - security/compliance vendor and speaker programme
why_relevant: Slovenia's main information-security conference; DORA/NIS2/ZInfV-1 tracks attract the ICT suppliers that serve banks. Sponsor and speaker lists snowball into the regtech/security vendor ecosystem selling into SI financial entities.

source_name: Računalniške novice - partner directory and event calendar (sl IT trade press)
why_relevant: Slovenian IT trade outlet that runs vendor profile pages (e.g. Halcom) and an events calendar. Good snowball surface for identifying SI IT suppliers with a finance practice and for catching vendor announcements that never reach English-language wires.

source_name: Uradni list RS - business/news section carrying vendor announcements
why_relevant: Beyond the official gazette, its news channel publishes vendor/company items (e.g. Halcom rebrand and digital-banking positioning). Provides a Slovenian-language, dated, archived record of supplier-side claims about the banking market.

source_name: Apps Run The World - NLB d.d. customer software purchase profile
why_relevant: Commercial IT-buyer database profiling NLB's software stack and digital-transformation purchases. Useful as a cross-check on which vendors claim NLB, though it is a paid aggregator and its entries must be corroborated against vendor primary sources.

source_name: Fintech trade wires (Finextra, The Paypers, FinTech Futures) - Slovenia/Bankart coverage
why_relevant: These wires reliably pick up SI vendor-bank deals (Bankart-Nets instant payments 2019, Bankart-Diebold Nixdorf 2024) and often add context the vendor release omits. Best single early-warning net for supplier-side signals about Slovenian banks.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. - company site (supplier-side counterparty for all SI banks)
why_relevant: Bankart is the shared card/payment processor for the Slovenian banking sector and is itself the buyer in most vendor announcements. Its own site (sl and en) identifies participating banks, services and platform changes, and is the hinge that turns one vendor announcement into sector-wide regulatory-project intelligence.

source_name: NLB Group - sporočila za javnost / press releases (technology and partner announcements)
why_relevant: The bank side of vendor announcements. NLB publicises technology programmes (e.g. its fintech architecture being a 2021 Gartner Eye on Innovation finalist) that name or imply suppliers, and its releases date programmes that vendors later cite as references.

source_name: Microsoft Trust Center - DORA compliance (Slovenian localisation)
why_relevant: Hyperscalers are DORA-designated ICT third-party providers to SI banks. Their sl-SI compliance pages and contractual addenda document exactly which DORA articles they cover for financial-entity customers - the supplier-side evidence of cloud dependency at private SI banks.
